# RELEASE


## DETAILS


## Uniti Demonstrates Industry’s First Single-Fiber 800G Service, Simplifying High-Capacity Connectivity for Customers


November 12, 2026


[PDF Version](https://investor.uniti.com/node/17026/pdf)


- Trial with Nokia validates 800GbE service with an efficient 800GE client handoff over a single fiber pair
- Creates a simpler, more efficient way for customers to access high-capacity connectivity


LITTLE ROCK, Ark., Nov. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Uniti Wholesale, a leading provider of advanced fiber infrastructure solutions, today announced the successful trial of an industry first 800 Gigabit Ethernet (800GE) service delivered with a single fiber pair demarcation to the customer. The milestone demonstrates a simpler and more efficient way for customers to access 800G connectivity as demand for high-capacity network services continues to grow.


Conducted between Chicago, Ill., and Lexington, Ky., the trial demonstrated an 800GE service using the Nokia 1830 Global Express (GX) solution, establishing a single fiber 800G connectivity (IEEE 802.3dj 800GBASE-LR4). Unlike other available 800GE client interfaces that rely on multiple fiber pairs, the trial validates that Uniti can provide the complete 800G customer handoff over a single fiber pair.


The successful trial underscores Uniti’s continued investment in next-generation network capabilities and provides a foundation for delivering higher-capacity services through a customer interface designed to simplify access to 800G connectivity.


“Our customers are looking for more capacity, but they also want the experience of connecting to that capacity to be as simple and efficient as possible,” said Greg Ortyl, executive vice president and president of strategic accounts for Uniti Wholesale. “By demonstrating an 800G service with a single fiber pair handoff, we are simplifying the customer connection while giving businesses a straightforward path to the next generation of high-capacity connectivity. This industry-first achievement reflects our focus on making advanced network technology easier for our customers to access.”


“AI and cloud are driving unprecedented growth in data and creating demand for faster, more scalable connectivity across data centers, clouds and networks,” said Scott Cohen, senior vice president and North America Region leader at Nokia. “As capacity grows, the industry also needs simpler ways to access that bandwidth without adding operational complexity. Working with Uniti to demonstrate a single fiber 800G service is a great example of how optical innovation can increase network capacity into simpler, more efficient connectivity for customers.”


Uniti Wholesale expects to make the 800G service available to customers in the first quarter of 2027.
